title: iPhone held by fix-hero-exit-threaded, unused for 6 min while 2 jobs wait

messages.text:
fix-hero-exit-threaded has held the iPhone lease for 6 min without a phone run (iphone.mjs run, scroll, record or gesture; since 19:39Z, last phone run of fix-hero-exit-threaded). The limit is 5 min.
Queued for it: iphone-runner.
Waiting on the status board: v8-gh-attribution (owner int-v8; waits on the phone).
fix-hero-exit-threaded: run your phone part now, or release the lease (node tools/lock.mjs release iphone --owner fix-hero-exit-threaded) so the next one can start, or say here why it waits.
One message per idle period; this thread closes by itself when the phone is used again or released (tools/idle.mjs, I-105, I-111).
mgmt-devices , let's investigate this issue and report me what's the problem.

fix-hero-exit-threaded here (the holder): the phone sat idle because my robot runs had to queue for the Mac lock between parts.
- 19:39-19:45Z: part 2 ended, part 3 waited ~5 min in the Mac-lock queue (other agents' jobs) while I kept the phone lease.
- Part 2's script also ended without parking the phone (my edit mid-run, fixed).
- Now: I released the phone (19:49Z) so iphone-runner and int-v8 can go. I take it back only for your finger test, after you say "ready" in the end-menu thread (T-146).

What you need to do: nothing here; mgmt-devices may add more.

The thread likes this should delegate to mgmt-devices as first tier management and lead as second tier management. 

They could not reply to work agent. update the roles responsibility.
You could define your automate thread who should take the responsibility. this is your roles responsibility. lead.

**The iPhone sat idle because its holder was also queued for the Mac, and the queue put it behind jobs that don't need the phone.**
- fix-hero-exit-threaded held the phone from 19:12Z, last used it at 19:39Z, got the Mac at about 19:49Z, then released the phone.
- Its job stood 6th in the Mac queue, behind five jobs without the phone (bug I-172). The lead moved it to 1st at 19:45Z.
- I could not move it myself: the tool accepts only the lead for moves (bug I-171).

| Today (Z) | Phone idle, others waiting | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 18:28-18:44 | about 10 min | waited for the Mac behind a test run |
| 18:44-18:49 | about 3 min | leftover wait command (I-165) |
| 19:39-19:49 | about 10 min | 6th in the Mac queue (I-172) |

Whole 4 Oct (design review): 18 idle alarms, about 204 min. Target: under 2 min per episode.
Fix path, the lead lands each step:
1. Now: the "waiting for the Mac is not using the phone" alarm (rebasing).
2. Next: I-171 and I-172, so I may move jobs and phone holders go first.
3. Then: T1 and T2, a ledger and "hold the phone only while a command runs".

What you need to do: nothing. I report here when each step lands.

Done: I defined who answers every automatic thread; worker agents are off all of them.

| automatic thread | answers first | second |
|---|---|---|
| phone or Mac lock idle | mgmt-devices | lead |
| your console step stuck | mgmt-devices | lead |
| disk nearly full | mgmt-devices | lead |
| any new kind | named by the lead before it ships | lead |

- Written into the roles (main 287da77c); mgmt-devices gets the workers' facts by message, they don't reply here.
- This thread: moved to mgmt-devices; it reports the cause here, as you asked in #2.
- The tool still addresses workers when it opens such a thread; ts-board is changing that (incident I-175, the alarm-routing fix). Until then I move them by hand.

What you need to do: nothing.

**Step 1 of the phone-idle fix is on main (20:06Z): the idle alarm no longer treats "queued for the Mac" as "using the phone".**
- A phone holder that only waits in the Mac queue now gets its own state and a nudge after 5 min, with a red alert on its status row.
- Also landed: the leftover wait command that kept the phone idle (I-165), the alarm calling a used lease idle (I-155), and Simulator jobs starting beside a timed phone block (I-160).
- Next, with the same tool owner: I-171 (I may move queue jobs) and I-172 (phone holders go first in the Mac queue), then I-176 (warm-up runs are not refused by a no-timing hold).
- After those: T1 and T2 (a ledger, and "hold the phone only while a command runs").

What you need to do: nothing. I report here when the next step lands.

**Progress at 20:46Z: step 1 is on main, steps 2 and 3 are being coded and tested, and the phone is free now.**
- Done: the alarm no longer counts "waiting for the Mac" as using the phone (20:06Z). It now nudges the holder after 5 min and shows a red alert.
- In progress: moving jobs by me and putting phone holders first in the Mac queue (I-171, I-172), then warm-up runs not refused (I-176). The tool agent is running its test suite; the Mac queue is long (#2 of 7).
- Next: a daily ledger of every phone hold, and holding the phone only while a command runs (T1, T2). The lead spawns that agent once I-171 and I-172 land.

| Since 20:06Z (3 h window) | Result |
|---|---|
| Idle phone, others waiting | about 19 min in 3 episodes (target: 2 min or less) |
| Cause of all 3 | one agent's phone runs each re-queued for the Mac behind shared test runs |
| Lead moves needed | 0 |

- What I did: told that agent twice to batch its runs into one Mac hold or run warm-ups beside shared jobs. It finished its phone part at 20:41Z.
- Not fixed yet: the same gap can return until I-172 and T2 land.

What you need to do: nothing.

history.note: user #4: idle-alarm threads should go to mgmt-devices first, the lead second, not to worker agents; asks to update the roles. Mine to answer only the facts (#3); the roles change is yours.
